newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy defends conduct of Albania evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Italy defends conduct of Albania evacuation.

text.p: Italy on Saturday defended the conduct of its military evacuation of foreigners from Albania after furious complaints from rescued Britons that Italian troops had left them for hours at the mercy of an armed mob.

Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told parliament that the air and sea rescue, which brought out a total of 1,200 foreigners and Albanians in various missions, had been carried out in exemplary fashion by the forces involved.
He said the ministry was investigating allegations from some of the Britons that Italian soldiers had shot dead at least one Albanian in a gun battle on Thursday night at the port of Durres.
"We are ascertaining the facts but we do not have direct knowledge of episodes of that kind. There was shooting in the port that night but not in the area controlled by our men," Andreatta said.

The Britons said the Italians, including troops from the crack San Marco Battalion, retreated out to sea after the shoot-out and did not return until after dawn to pick them up, leaving them in terror.

Sixty-four Britons were among more than 850 people, half of them Albanians, evacuated to southeast Italy on Friday on the amphibious assault ship San Giusto after being rescued by helicopter from Tirana or by landing craft at Durres.
Andreatta said several foreign governments had thanked Italy for the way it brought their citizens to safety.
"The evacuation operations of civilians were conducted with exemplary professionalism by our military forces but certainly they weren't there for a day out," Andreatta said.
"Our men...were exposed to fire several times," Andreatta said, adding that they had "always kept strong nerves and the ability to assess the situation they found themselves in."

Britain on Friday expressed "delight" at the success of the Durres evacuation. Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Saturday he was "naturally concerned" about the reported incident but noted that the evacuees had got out safely.

"There were large numbers of people milling around on the beach, including many Albanians, some of whom were violent, some of whom were themselves trying to flee," Rifkind told BBC radio in an interview.

"So it clearly was a difficult operation, but I'm sure the Italian authorities will want to examine whether there were any lessons to be learned from the way in which it was done for the future," he said.
